title: Keeping a running total
objectives: Add several numbers by pairing them into whole tens
Hold a running total across a chain of additions and subtractions
Check a total with a rounded estimate

screens.title: Keeping a running total
screens.prose: A trader adds up fills, profits and positions all day. We will add long chains by pairing numbers and keeping one total in mind.
Four numbers to add. You may add them in any order you like.
screens.question: What is $17 + 26 + 13 + 34$?

hints.text: Do any two of them make a whole ten?
17 and 13 end in 7 and 3.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Try pairing numbers whose units make 10.

byKey.lost-ten: You dropped a ten on the way. Pair them instead: $17 + 13 = 30$ and $26 + 34 = 60$.
byKey.extra-ten: You carried one ten too many. Pair them instead: $17 + 13 = 30$ and $26 + 34 = 60$.

explain.text: 17 and 13 make 30, and 26 and 34 make 60. Units that add to 10 pair into whole tens. Then $30 + 60 = 90$ is easy.

screens.prose: Five numbers. Four of them pair up into whole tens. Look for units that add to 10.
screens.question: Tap the one number with no partner.

hints.text: Which units digits add to 10: 8, 5, 2, 5, 2?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Pair 18 with 22 and 25 with 15. What is left?

explain.text: $18 + 22 = 40$ and $25 + 15 = 40$. The 32 is left over, so the total is $40 + 40 + 32 = 112$.

screens.prose: Some chains mix adding and taking away. Keep one number, the **running total**, and change it at each step. Here: $46 + 27 - 18 + 35$.
screens.question: The total so far is 55. Add the 35. Where does the chain end?

hints.text: Start from the latest stop, 55.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add 35 to the latest total, 55.

byKey.restart: You added 35 to 73, the total before the $-18$. Each step changes the latest total, which is 55.
byKey.lost-ten: $55 + 30 = 85$, and the last 5 bridges to 90. You lost the ten from $5 + 5$.

explain.text: You held one number and changed it three times: 73, 55, 90. Only the latest total matters. The earlier stops can be forgotten.

screens.prose: Fill in the running total after each step. Use any trick from this level: from the left, round and adjust, or count up.
screens.question: Fill in the running total.

hints.text: Work down one row at a time, starting from the row above.
For $-29$, take away 30 and give 1 back.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each row changes the total in the row above.

byKey.r1c1: The first step starts from 0, so the total is just 38.
byKey.r2c1: $38 - 12$: take 10 to get 28, then 2 more to get 26.
byKey.r4c1: $71 - 29$: take 30 to get 41, then give 1 back to get 42.

explain.text: Each row used only the row above it. That is all a running total asks: one number held, one step at a time.

canvas.caption: The total visits 38, 26, 71, 42 and ends at 99

screens.prose: A friend adds $48 + 31 + 67 + 22$ and gets 146. A quick check: round each number to the nearest ten, then add.
screens.question: What is the rounded estimate?

hints.text: 48 rounds to 50. What do the others round to?
31 rounds to 30, 67 to 70 and 22 to 20.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Round each number to its nearest ten, then add.

byKey.down: You rounded every number down. 48 and 67 are nearer 50 and 70.
byKey.exact: 168 is the exact total. The estimate rounds first, so it is 170, and it is much quicker to find.

explain.text: The estimate is 170. Rounding moved the numbers by 2, 1, 3 and 2, at most 8 in all. 146 is 24 below 170, so it is wrong: your friend left out the 22, and the true total is 168.

canvas.caption: The true total must lie in the band. 146 does not.

screens.prose: A running total can fall below zero. Start at 0, then $+35$, then $-52$, then $+28$.
screens.question: Where does the running total end?

hints.text: $35 - 52$: how far below zero does it go?
From $-17$, 17 brings you to 0, and the last 11 lands on 11.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Go step by step: 35, then take 52, then add 28.

byKey.signs: You added 17 and 28. The total was $-17$, below zero, so 28 brings it back up past zero.
byKey.kept-minus: From $-17$, adding 28 climbs 17 to reach 0, then 11 more. The answer is above zero.

explain.text: The total went 35, then $-17$, then 11. Below zero, count up to 0 first, then carry on. That is the edge case: zero is just one more ten to bridge.

screens.prose: Pairing is quick, but watch the signs. Cara sees $70 - 18 + 12$. She pairs 18 with 12 to make 30 and takes it away: 40.
screens.question: What is $70 - 18 + 12$?

options.why: That is Cara's answer. She took away the 12 as well, but the 12 is added.
You added all three. The 18 is taken away.

hints.text: Which numbers are added and which are taken away?
Only the 18 is taken away.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Keep each sign with its own number.

byKey.b: You paired the two numbers as if both were taken away. Keep each sign with its number: $-18 + 12 = -6$, then $70 - 6 = 64$.

explain.text: Each number carries its own sign. You can pair $-18$ with $+12$ to make $-6$, or go step by step: 52, then 64. Pairing across a minus sign is safe only when the signs come along.

screens.prose: Two habits make a long chain safe. Add in any order, with each number keeping its own sign: $$a - b + c = a + (c - b)$$ Then carry one running total, and check the end with a rounded estimate.
screens.question: In $63 - 27 + 17$, which pair makes a whole ten?

options.why: You dropped the minus sign on 27. It is taken away, so pair it as $-27$.
You paired 63 with 27 as if both were added. The 27 is taken away.

hints.text: Which number has a minus sign in front of it?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Keep the minus sign with the 27.

explain.text: $-27$ and $+17$ make $-10$, so the chain is $63 - 10 = 53$. Step by step agrees: $63 - 27 = 36$, then $36 + 17 = 53$.

screens.title: Ten against the clock
screens.prose: Ten sums from this level. Start a timer, fill in all ten, then stop it. Note your time, and try to beat it next session.
screens.question: Fill in all ten answers.

hints.text: Pick a method for each sum before you start it.
Near a ten, round and adjust. For a subtraction, count up.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The amber cells need another look.

byKey.r5c1: Take 40 to get 53, then give 2 back.
byKey.r6c1: Add 100 to get 135, then take 2 off.
byKey.r9c1: Take 100 to get 45, then give 1 back.

explain.text: Each sum used one move from this level: from the left, round and adjust, or count up. Speed comes from choosing the move at a glance. The daily warm-up will keep timing you.

screens.prose: Your profit and loss, or **P&L**, on four trades today. Keep a running total after each trade, as a trading desk does.
screens.question: Fill in the running P&L, in pounds.

hints.text: After trade 1, the running P&L is just that trade's P&L.
£7.85 is 15p less than £8.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each row changes the total in the row above by one trade.

byKey.r0c2: After one trade the total is just that trade's P&L, £12.40.
byKey.r3c2: £27.65 − £15.65: the pence cancel, so it is £27 − £15 = £12.00.

explain.text: Each row changed the total by one trade. The day ends £12.00 up, though it was only £4.55 up after trade 2. A desk watches this running number all day.

ideas: Numbers whose units add to 10 pair into whole tens.
A running total holds one number and changes it at each step.
A rounded estimate catches a total that is far too big or too small.
summary.trap: Pairing two numbers across a minus sign and taking both away.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Pair the two numbers whose units make 10.

byKey.lost-ten: You dropped a ten. Pair 24 with 16 to make 40, then add 38.

explain.text: 24 and 16 pair up to make 40. Then $40 + 38 = 78$.

quiz.prose: During the morning you buy 35 shares, sell 18, buy 27 and sell 40.
quiz.question: How many shares do you hold now?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Buys add to the position and sells take away from it.

byKey.all-added: You added every trade. Sells take shares away from the position.
byKey.sign: You bought 62 shares and sold 58, so you hold more than none: 4, not −4.

explain.text: The running position goes 35, 17, 44, 4. Or pair the buys and the sells: bought $35 + 27 = 62$, sold $18 + 40 = 58$, so you hold 4.

options.why: You paired 26 with 14 and took both away. The 14 is added.
You added all three. The 26 is taken away.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Keep each sign with its own number.

explain.text: $-26$ and $+14$ make $-12$, so the chain is $90 - 12 = 78$. Step by step: 64, then 78.

quiz.question: What does a rounded estimate say about 170?

options.text: It must be wrong: the estimate is 190, and rounding moved the total by at most 6
It could be right: it is within 20 of the estimate
options.why: You allowed too much slack. Each number moved by at most 2 when rounded, so the total can be off by no more than 6.

options.text: It could be right: it ends in 0, like the estimate
options.why: The last digit is not a check of size. 170 is 20 below the estimate of 190.

feedback.correct: 190, and 170 is too far from it.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Round each number to its nearest ten and compare.

explain.text: $30 + 50 + 40 + 70 = 190$. Rounding moved the numbers by 1, 2, 2 and 1, at most 6 in all. 170 is 20 away, so it is wrong; the true total is 190.
